description: EARTH.exe is a six-member team from Bangladesh developing BoponX, a NASA-data-powered solution for climate-resilient farming.
summary: BoponX ("From Space to Soil / মহাকাশ থেকে মাটিতে") is a bilingual (Bangla/English) agricultural decision-support platform and voice-enabled AI Field Assistant built for Bangladesh's 16.5 million smallholder farming households and extension officers across all 64 districts. Smallholder farmers face shifting monsoon and rabi rainfall onsets, unseasonal heatwaves, coastal salinity intrusion, and Bay of Bengal cyclones, making static historical planting calendars unreliable while raw NASA satellite portals remain too technical for field use. BoponX solves the "Field Shift" challenge through a three-stage workflow: (1) an interactive 3D/2D Earth Twin fusing six NASA satellite systems (NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, SMAP L3, GIBS/MODIS, SRTM, and EONET v3) with six Bangladesh agricultural authorities (BAMIS, BARC, SRDI, BARI, BRRI, and DAE 16123); (2) a non-parametric 26-year rainfall onset-shift analyzer and an HTTP 422 Soil Evidence Gate that blocks unsafe fertilizer guessing without soil tests; and (3) a 90-day printable A4 field plan, 160-character GSM-7 SMS advisory, and conversational AI assistant tested directly with farmers in Rajshahi, Bangladesh.
details:
1. What BoponX Does & How It Works

BoponX ("From Space to Soil") translates complex NASA Earth observation streams and official Bangladesh agronomic standards into auditable, 90-day field actions across a 3-stage workflow:

Stage 01 — Locate (3D Earth Twin & Live Telemetry): Farmers or Sub-Assistant Agriculture Officers (SAAOs) pick any GPS point or select from all 64 Bangladesh districts on an interactive 3D Globe and 2D map displaying 6 live NASA GIBS satellite layers (MODIS TrueColor, MODIS NDVI 250m, MODIS Day LST 1km, GPM IMERG Precipitation, SMAP L3 Soil Moisture, and SRTM 30m DEM). The backend fetches 14-day live agroclimatology and 20-year climatology normals from NASA POWER alongside active cyclone, flood, and storm alerts within 1,200 km from NASA EONET v3.

Stage 02 — Analyze (26-Year Onset-Shift Lab & HTTP 422 Soil Evidence Gate): Our engine analyzes 26 years (2000–2025) of daily NASA POWER rainfall across 40 native MERRA-2 grid cells using non-parametric Mann-Whitney U tests, Hodges-Lehmann median shift estimators, and 1,000-iteration bootstrap 95% confidence intervals to quantify how many days usable sowing rain has shifted compared to official BAMIS calendars. Interactive What-If sliders let farmers simulate rainfall (-50% to +50%) and heat (0°C to +6°C) shocks across 3-crop rotations using BARI and BRRI FAO-56 crop water coefficients (ETc = ETo × Kc). Crucially, BoponX enforces an HTTP 422 Soil Evidence Gate: because satellites sense physical wetness (0–100 cm) rather than chemical pH, salinity (EC dS/m), or NPK nutrients, BoponX refuses to guess chemical fertilizer doses until verified SRDI or lab soil inputs unlock BARC FRG-2024 split NPK schedules.

Stage 03 — Action (90-Day Printable Plan, SMS & Voice AI Assistant): Produces a 3-phase 90-day checklist (Days 1–30 Establishment, Days 31–60 Vegetative, Days 61–90 Maturity) where every task cites its exact NASA or local rule provenance, exports a 4-page printable A4 PDF field sheet, formats a <160-character GSM-7/Bangla SMS with DAE Krishi Call Center (16123) sign-off, and provides a bilingual BoponX AI Field Assistant with voice-to-text and audio read-aloud.

2. Key Benefits & Intended Impact

Prevents Premature Sowing & Crop Loss: Quantifies multi-decade rainfall onset shifts at the district level so farmers avoid false-start rains or late-season terminal heat stress on Boro/Aman rice, mustard, wheat, lentil, maize, mungbean, and jute.

Stops Unsafe Fertilizer Guessing: Protects soil health and farmer budgets by separating satellite physical soil moisture from laboratory chemical fertility.

Bridges the Digital Divide: Reaches both smartphone users (via 3D/2D maps and Bangla voice assistant) and offline rural farmers (via printable A4 paper plans and <160-char SMS advisories), validated directly in the field with farmers in Rajshahi, Bangladesh.

3. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

Backend & Scientific Computing: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, NumPy/SciPy statistical methods (Mann-Whitney U, Hodges-Lehmann, Pearson r), httpx async clients, Earthdata OPeNDAP (GPM_3IMERGDF / GPM_3IMERGDE V07), and Pytest (133 automated unit and scientific validation tests).

Frontend & Geospatial Visualization: TypeScript, React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js / react-globe.gl (3D Earth Twin), Leaflet (2D satellite tile overlays), and Browser Web Speech API (SpeechRecognition & speechSynthesis).

4. How BoponX Is Creative & Factors Considered

Zero-Fabrication Scientific Guardrails: Unlike black-box AI wrappers, BoponX never invents weather data on upstream outage (HTTP 503), cross-validates NASA POWER against NASA GPM IMERG V07 (reporting Mean Bias, MAE, RMSE, and Pearson r), and enforces the HTTP 422 physical-vs.-chemical soil boundary.

Human-Centered Rural Design: Our team considered literacy, language, mobile screen constraints, and rural connectivity across Bangladesh—building a one-click Bangla/English toggle, voice commands, printable paper plans, and direct escalation to Bangladesh's toll-free 16123 extension helpline.

5. Super Intelligence (SI) & AI Disclosure

In-App AI Assistant (/api/v1/chat): Uses a deterministic agronomic rule engine with optional OpenAI-compatible LLM reasoning strictly grounded in live NASA/local runtime telemetry and bounded by our HTTP 422 soil gate.

Video & Audio: Selected illustrative B-roll clips in our video are generated with AI video tools and carry a visible on-screen watermark ("This part AI-Generated."), while all software demonstrations and Rajshahi farmer interviews are authentic recordings. Browser Web Speech synthesis provides in-app accessibility read-aloud.

Code & Documentation: AI coding assistants were used to accelerate UI scaffolding, bilingual translation polishing, and documentation formatting; all scientific algorithms and tests were authored and verified by Team EARTH.exe (Rezwan Hossain Prince, Shafayet Hossain, Md. Khairul Islam Joy, Tulip Mondal Gourab, Alana Mondal Roshni, and Iftekar Azad Ether).
